I'd try a different approach -

Get a piece of plate glass cut from a glass/window show at least 1/4" thick and whatever size your like, maybe 6" x 12". Make a stand-up border around the edge w/ RTV (silicone caulk) then wipe silicone lube on the glass. Cut off a chunk of wax, melt it on the stove, then pour it on the glass until the thickness is beyond what you need. It will shrink as it cools but you should be able to get close to your final thickness. Since the wax is tough you can sand it with 240 grit paper then use heat to smooth it out. Doing it this way you end up with a large sheet close to the thickness required.

The wax is definitely capable of being melted and poured into a mold.

Thank you for the suggestion!

If you use glass as the mold base one face will be quite flat and not need much work to smooth. The silicone lube acts as a release agent so the wax sheet comes up easily. You may need to experiment, if that does not work well try powdered graphite (messy but nothing sticks to it).
